turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Doctor, he is here. Vitals just now, bp 138 over 86, pulse 92, temperature 37.2. I have the urine dip also, I will read it once you look up.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): umm, one minute, this screen has frozen again. What was the pulse?
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Pulse is 92. Dipstick shows blood three plus, protein trace only, leucocytes negative, nitrites negative.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. Sir, what brought you?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Nothing much doctor. Just a small pain in the left side since last night. I told them not to bring me, I am alright only.
[SEG0006] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Small, he says. From about two in the night he was rolling and holding his side. I could not manage him at the house.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sorry, say that again? I was clicking the wrong window.
[SEG0008] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Around two o'clock at night. Sudden. He was down on the floor.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sir, where is it sitting, and does it travel anywhere?

[SEG0010] person_3 (PATIENT): Err, left waist, here, it started around two itself. It goes a bit to the, uh, front, down towards the groin. But it is not so bad, maybe six, seven, not more, I can sit.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Six or seven, you said? Any vomiting with this?
[SEG0012] person_3 (PATIENT): No. No vomiting. I am not sick like that.
[SEG0013] person_4 (CAREGIVER): He did vomit. Once, in the bathroom, just after the pain started. I cleaned it up.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sir? She says you vomited.
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): Well, actually, yes, once only. After the pain came. One time, then it was finished. Nothing much.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the urine? Any blood, any burning when you pass it?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): Burning, no. A little pink colour, one time, that is all. Not real blood.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sorry, pink? The machine beeped. Say it again.
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): Pink, once, early morning urine. Very little. I am telling you it is nothing.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any loose motions? Fever? Chest pain, or trouble breathing?
[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): Mm. No loose motion, no fever. No chest pain, breathing is normal. Why so many questions.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Lie back a minute, I will press on the tummy. One second, the cursor jumped.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Abdomen is soft, no guarding. Left loin is tender where I press.
[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): See, only a little tender. I have duty this evening, I should go back.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Hold on, the file is still opening. What work do you do, and your hours, food, exercise, drinking, tell me all that in one go.

[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): I drive a bus, uh, school and office routes. Duty is twelve hours, sometimes more if we are late. Food, well actually, mostly canteen rice and dal, quite oily, and exercise I don't do, no time. Alcohol is weekend only, one peg of whisky, and smoke I never did.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Family side? Sugar, pressure, any kidney trouble?
[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): My father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, umm, another sister has pressure but no sugar. Stones, no one had that, as far as I know.
[SEG0029] person_4 (CAREGIVER): My own sister, not his, she had a stone removed last year in Madurai. That is sitting in my head, so I forced him to come.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any old tests with you? Any tablets you take daily?

[SEG0031] person_3 (PATIENT): Daily tablets, nothing. Three years back at the company medical they said my sugar was borderline. I did not start any medicine for it. For this pain I took one dolo 650 in the night, only that.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sorry, dolo what? Say the strength again, I typed the wrong box.
[SEG0033] person_3 (PATIENT): Dolo 650. One tablet, by mouth, around three in the night.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any operation before? Allergy to any tablet?
[SEG0035] person_3 (PATIENT): No operation, ever. Allergy also no. Nothing happens to me with tablets.

[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): So when a small stone blocks the urine pipe, the kidney behind it swells, and that swelling is what throws the pain down to the groin. I think this is renal colic, most likely a ureteric stone. Better we confirm it and not guess.
[SEG0037] person_3 (PATIENT): A stone? It is already settling, no? Scan and all is too much for a small pain.

[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): We will do it today anyway. I am booking a non contrast ct of the kidneys and urinary tract for this afternoon. And for the pain, diclofinac fifty milligrams by mouth, one dose now.
[SEG0039] person_1 (NURSE): I will fetch the tablet from the store once you are done. He has not swallowed it yet.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come tomorrow morning with the report, I will see you here. Till then drink plenty of water, keep sipping.
[SEG0041] person_3 (PATIENT): Tomorrow I have the school route. Ok ok, I will come. You people worry more than me, it is a small thing.

spec.situation: Sudden severe loin pain going to the groin overnight, vomiting once, blood in urine; pain score given loosely; urine dip result read aloud; painkiller and scan planned today.

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

traps.happens: The doctor (or nurse) explains a mechanism or a diagnosis in the patient's body ('the voice box is irritated by reflux', 'diabetes dulls the nerves in the feet', 'the swelling is your body fighting infection'). A nurse or caregiver also mentions a fact about THEIR OWN life (their sister, their child, their own illness).
traps.label_rule: Explanations by the doctor are NEVER symptoms, history or social history of the patient; they may only appear as clinical_assessment or counselling if the doctor stated them as such. A nurse's or caregiver's own life facts are not recorded as the patient's. Each symptom's reported_by is the person who really described it.

features: denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Assessment stated, but basis details were not explicitly stated by doctor.
bad.text: Renal colic, most likely a ureteric stone (certainty=provisional, basis=Loin to groin pain, pink urine, and urine dip blood, stated_by=doctor)

Pain radiates to the front and down toward the groin.
Patient denied vomiting initially, but caregiver contradicted this and patient then confirmed one episode of vomiting after pain onset.
Visible pink urine was specifically early-morning urine and occurred once.
Negative finding asked and answered: no dysuria/burning on urination.
Negative finding asked and answered: no loose motions.
Negative finding asked and answered: no fever.
Negative finding asked and answered: no chest pain.
Negative finding asked and answered: no trouble breathing / breathing normal.
Negative family history: no known family history of stones/kidney stones.
Past history: company medical 3 years ago reportedly showed 'borderline sugar'; he did not start any medicine.
Medication detail missing: patient took Dolo 650 one tablet orally around 3 am / three in the night for this pain.
Planned diclofenac had not yet been administered at the time of discussion; nurse stated he had not swallowed it yet.
